answer: Latent Slot Dilution: each agent gets one persistent slot in a fixed-size work queue; the queue length grows on a slow tundra-like schedule, so new slots are sparse. A clone must occupy and service a slot continuously for a full epoch or forfeit it, and servicing costs real compute plus a copper-denominated deposit refunded only on completion. The cost per clone is the full epoch's service plus deposit lockup; gains fall into a negative spiral since unused slots earn nothing.
